brief: BTIG's technical strategy note flags unusually low SPY trading volume: Friday's 22.6 million shares was the lowest since the 12/24/19 half-day, the lowest full trading day since 11/25/05, and the lowest non-holiday day since 10/11/04; today is on pace for roughly 19 million shares, which would be the lowest non-holiday volume since 2003. BTIG attributes this to a calendar lull between macro catalysts and earnings season. Broader NYSE Composite volume reads less extreme, below its 20-day average but above August levels. The 5-day average SPY volume is set to finish near 31 million, only the fourth time since 2005 it has fallen below 35 million; the prior three instances (Dec. 2024, Feb. 2025, Aug. 2026) each preceded SPY weakening in short order. SPX has gone 52 sessions without a -1% day, tying a streak from July 2024, and the NYSE has gone nearly a year without an 80%+ downside-volume day. BTIG expects volume and volatility to rise as earnings season intensifies and expects SPY to weaken as it did in the prior three low-volume episodes.
